entries.name: Buttermilk
entries.role_in_recipes: Adds acidity and tenderness; its acid activates baking soda for lift.

subs.name: Milk + lemon juice or vinegar
subs.use: 1 Tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar + enough milk to reach 1 cup; rest 10 min
subs.function_note: The acid curdles the milk, mimicking buttermilk's tang and soda-reactivity.

subs.name: Plain yogurt, thinned
subs.use: 3/4 cup plain yogurt + 1/4 cup milk, whisked smooth
subs.function_note: Cultured yogurt carries the same lactic acid tang.

subs.name: Soy or almond milk + acid
subs.use: 1 Tbsp lemon juice or vinegar + enough soy or almond milk to reach 1 cup; rest 10 min
subs.function_note: The acid curdles plant milk the same way.

subs.name: Milk + cream of tartar
subs.use: 1 3/4 tsp cream of tartar + enough milk to reach 1 cup
subs.metric_use: 8 g cream of tartar + 240 ml milk
subs.function_note: Cream of tartar is a dry acid — same reaction, no added flavor.

entries.name: Eggs
entries.role_in_recipes: Binds, leavens, adds moisture and structure; sets when heated.

subs.name: Flax egg
subs.use: 1 Tbsp ground flaxseed + 3 Tbsp water; rest 10 min until gelled
subs.function_note: Ground flax mucilage gels like egg white.
subs.tradeoffs: Binds but doesn't leaven; bakes denser

subs.name: Water + oil + baking powder
subs.use: 1 1/2 Tbsp water + 1 1/2 Tbsp oil + 1 tsp baking powder
subs.metric_use: 22 ml water + 22 ml oil + 4 g baking powder
subs.function_note: Oil adds the moisture; baking powder supplies the lift.

subs.name: Unsweetened applesauce
subs.function_note: Pectin and fiber bind moisture.

subs.name: Aquafaba (chickpea liquid)
subs.use: 3 Tbsp aquafaba (2 Tbsp in place of 1 egg white); whips to peaks
subs.function_note: Chickpea cooking water carries proteins that whip like egg white.
subs.tradeoffs: Whips faster but is less stable than whites

subs.name: Plain yogurt
subs.function_note: Yogurt adds moisture and binding; no leavening.

entries.name: Butter
entries.role_in_recipes: Adds fat, flavor, and lift (creamed with sugar); browns and crisps.

subs.name: Olive or vegetable oil
subs.function_note: Oil is 100% fat vs butter's ~80%.
subs.tradeoffs: Cookies spread more; cakes moister but less airy; no butter flavor

subs.name: Coconut oil
subs.use: 1 cup coconut oil, solid (refined for neutral flavor)
subs.function_note: Same solid-at-room-temperature fat behavior.

subs.name: Applesauce (half swap)
subs.use: Replace up to HALF the butter with applesauce (1/2 cup butter = 1/2 cup applesauce)
subs.metric_use: 1:1 by volume for the replaced half
subs.function_note: Pectin holds the moisture fat would.
subs.avoid_if: cookies, pie crust, or anything that needs creaming for lift
subs.tradeoffs: Denser and very moist; less richness

subs.name: Vegan butter / margarine
subs.function_note: Engineered to match butter's fat-water ratio.

entries.name: Heavy cream
entries.role_in_recipes: Adds ~36% fat for richness; whips into peaks; thickens sauces.

subs.name: Milk + melted butter
subs.function_note: Rebuilds the fat content; whipping needs real cream's emulsion.

subs.name: Chilled coconut cream
subs.function_note: High fat traps air once chilled and whipped.

subs.name: Half-and-half + butter
subs.function_note: Same fat math as milk plus butter.

entries.name: Milk
entries.role_in_recipes: Adds moisture, mild sweetness, and protein for browning.

subs.name: Soy or oat milk
subs.use: 1 cup unsweetened soy or oat milk
subs.function_note: Fortified soy mirrors milk's proteins for browning.

subs.name: Water + butter
subs.function_note: Butter restores the milkfat; water replaces the liquid.

subs.name: Evaporated milk, diluted
subs.function_note: Evaporated milk is just concentrated milk.

entries.name: All-purpose flour
entries.role_in_recipes: Structure via gluten; the default protein (~10-12%) for most baking.

subs.name: Bread flour
subs.use: 1 cup bread flour — use slightly less liquid in the recipe
subs.function_note: Higher protein builds more gluten.

subs.name: Cake or pastry flour
subs.function_note: Lower protein makes less gluten.

subs.name: GF 1-to-1 baking blend
subs.use: 1 cup blend that contains xanthan gum
subs.function_note: Xanthan gum mimics gluten's binding.

entries.name: Cake flour
entries.role_in_recipes: Low protein (~8%) for tender, fine-crumbed cakes.

subs.name: AP flour + cornstarch
subs.use: 1 cup minus 2 Tbsp AP flour + 2 Tbsp cornstarch; sift twice
subs.function_note: Cornstarch dilutes AP's protein, limiting gluten.

entries.name: Bread flour
entries.role_in_recipes: High protein (~12-14%) develops strong gluten for chewy, tall breads.

subs.name: All-purpose flour
subs.function_note: AP's lower protein makes less gluten; knead 1-2 min longer.

subs.name: AP flour + vital wheat gluten
subs.use: 1 cup AP flour + 1 tsp vital wheat gluten
subs.function_note: Vital wheat gluten restores the protein gap directly.

entries.name: Self-rising flour
entries.role_in_recipes: AP flour pre-mixed with leavener and salt for biscuits and quick breads.

subs.name: AP flour + baking powder + salt
subs.use: 1 cup AP flour + 1 1/2 tsp baking powder + 1/4 tsp fine salt, whisked
subs.function_note: It is the same blend, made fresh.

entries.name: Baking powder
entries.role_in_recipes: Double-acting leavener: rises when wet AND when heated.

subs.name: Baking soda + cream of tartar
subs.use: 1/4 tsp baking soda + 1/2 tsp cream of tartar
subs.function_note: Cream of tartar is the dry acid that reacts with soda on contact.
subs.best_for: Batters headed straight to the oven

subs.name: Baking soda + acid in the recipe
subs.use: 1/4 tsp baking soda + swap the recipe's liquid for buttermilk or yogurt
subs.function_note: Buttermilk or yogurt supplies the acid the soda needs.

entries.name: Baking soda
entries.role_in_recipes: Base that reacts with recipe acids (buttermilk, brown sugar, yogurt) for lift.

subs.name: Baking powder (triple the amount)
subs.function_note: Powder carries its own acid; soda is 3-4x stronger.
subs.safety_note: Soda is 3-4x stronger than powder and needs recipe acid. Trippling powder adds a salty, metallic taste and less lift; best only in strongly acidic batters.

entries.name: Brown sugar
entries.role_in_recipes: White sugar + molasses: adds moisture, chew, and caramel depth.

subs.name: White sugar + molasses
subs.use: 1 cup white sugar + 1 Tbsp molasses (2 Tbsp for dark)
subs.function_note: Brown sugar IS white sugar plus molasses.

subs.name: White sugar
subs.use: 1 cup white sugar (result is crisper, less chewy)
subs.function_note: Molasses is what makes brown sugar soft and acidic.
subs.tradeoffs: Crisper, less chew, no caramel note

subs.name: Coconut sugar
subs.function_note: Unrefined cane sugar with natural molasses.

entries.name: Powdered sugar
entries.role_in_recipes: Finely ground sugar with cornstarch; dissolves instantly in frostings and glazes.

subs.name: Granulated sugar + cornstarch, blended
subs.use: 1 cup granulated sugar + 1 tsp cornstarch; blend until fine powder
subs.function_note: Blending fractures the crystals; cornstarch prevents caking.

entries.name: Honey
entries.role_in_recipes: Liquid sweetener; browns fast, holds moisture, adds floral flavor.

subs.name: Maple syrup
subs.use: 1 cup; lower oven 25 F and cut other liquid by 2 Tbsp
subs.function_note: Similar invert-sugar behavior.

subs.name: Light corn syrup
subs.function_note: Same liquid-sugar chemistry.

subs.name: Agave nectar
subs.use: 3/4 cup; cut other liquid by 2 Tbsp
subs.function_note: Higher fructose reads sweeter on the tongue.

entries.name: Maple syrup
entries.role_in_recipes: Liquid sweetener with distinct flavor; browns quickly.

subs.name: Honey
subs.function_note: Both are invert sugars.

subs.name: Brown sugar syrup
subs.use: Simmer 1 cup packed brown sugar + 1/4 cup water + 1/4 tsp vanilla until syrupy
subs.function_note: Dissolved brown sugar approximates syrup body.

entries.name: Corn syrup
entries.role_in_recipes: Invert sugar: prevents crystallization in candy, ganache, and brittle.

subs.name: Honey
subs.function_note: Invert sugars prevent crystallization.

subs.name: Golden syrup
subs.function_note: The closest chemistry match.

entries.name: Molasses
entries.role_in_recipes: Deep, bittersweet caramel notes; reacts with baking soda for lift in gingerbread.

subs.name: Dark corn syrup
subs.function_note: Similar body, less acidity — keep the baking soda.

subs.name: Brown sugar + water
subs.use: 3/4 cup packed brown sugar + 1/4 cup water, stirred
subs.function_note: Molasses dissolved into sugar approximates brown sugar.

entries.name: Cornstarch
entries.role_in_recipes: Pure starch thickener for sauces and puddings; tenderizer in cakes.

subs.name: Arrowroot powder
subs.use: 1 Tbsp arrowroot powder (1:1); stir in a slurry at the end, do not hard-boil
subs.function_note: Different starch chemistry — sets at a lower temperature.
subs.tradeoffs: Clearer, glossier; breaks if boiled hard

subs.name: Tapioca starch
subs.function_note: Same pure-starch behavior with more elasticity.

subs.name: All-purpose flour
subs.use: 2 Tbsp flour; cook 2-3 min longer to lose the raw taste
subs.function_note: Flour is only part starch — the rest is protein.
subs.tradeoffs: Cloudy; use double; raw taste if undercooked

entries.name: Cream of tartar
entries.role_in_recipes: Acid: stabilizes whipped egg whites and prevents sugar crystallization.

subs.name: Lemon juice or white vinegar
subs.use: 1/2 tsp lemon juice or white vinegar
subs.basis: per 1/4 tsp cream of tartar (per egg white)
subs.function_note: Any acid stabilizes whipped egg whites.

subs.name: Leave it out (chewy cookies only)
subs.function_note: In snickerdoodles it mostly provides tang and texture.
subs.tradeoffs: Slight loss of tang and chew

entries.name: Sour cream
entries.role_in_recipes: Cultured tang + fat: tenderizes cakes, enriches sauces and toppings.

subs.name: Greek yogurt (full fat)
subs.function_note: Same cultured-dairy chemistry.

subs.name: Crème fraîche
subs.function_note: Higher fat resists splitting under heat.

subs.name: Store-bought vegan sour cream
subs.use: 1 cup store-bought vegan sour cream (cashew or coconut base)
subs.function_note: Plant fats and cultures mimic the tang.

entries.name: Plain yogurt
entries.role_in_recipes: Tangy moisture and tenderizing acidity; marinade base.

subs.name: Sour cream, thinned
subs.function_note: Milk matches the consistency.

subs.name: Coconut yogurt
subs.function_note: Cultured plant base mirrors the acidity.

subs.name: Buttermilk (in batters/marinades)
subs.use: 1 cup buttermilk (slightly thinner; reduce other liquid by 1 Tbsp)
subs.function_note: Same lactic acid tenderizing.

entries.name: Cream cheese
entries.role_in_recipes: Tangy fat for frostings, cheesecakes, and sauces.

subs.name: Neufchâtel
subs.function_note: Same culture process, less cream.

subs.name: Strained Greek yogurt
subs.use: 1 cup Greek yogurt, strained 2 hrs in a cloth (for frostings and dips)
subs.function_note: Straining concentrates proteins to spreadable firmness.
subs.safety_note: Baked cheesecakes need cream cheese's fat and solids; strained yogurt makes a watery, curdled filling. Fine for no-bake or frosting use only.
subs.tradeoffs: Tangier; too soft for baked cheesecake

subs.name: Mascarpone
subs.use: 1 cup mascarpone + 1/4 tsp salt + 1 tsp lemon juice for tang
subs.function_note: Cream cheese's richer Italian cousin; add acid for tang.

entries.name: Half-and-half
entries.role_in_recipes: Half milk, half cream (~18% fat): coffee, sauces, custards.

subs.name: Milk + melted butter
subs.use: 1 Tbsp melted butter + enough milk to reach 1 cup
subs.function_note: Rebuilds the milkfat exactly.

subs.name: Whole milk
subs.function_note: Half the fat of half-and-half.

entries.name: Evaporated milk
entries.role_in_recipes: Concentrated milk (60% water removed): creamy without cream.

subs.name: Heavy cream
subs.function_note: Cream is simply fattier.

subs.name: Whole milk, simmered down
subs.use: Simmer 2 cups whole milk gently to 1 cup
subs.function_note: You are making evaporated milk from scratch.

entries.name: Sweetened condensed milk
entries.role_in_recipes: Sugar + concentrated milk: magic in fudge, bars, and dulce de leche.

subs.name: Milk + sugar, simmered
subs.use: Simmer 2 cups whole milk + 2/3 cup sugar, stirring, until reduced to 1 cup
subs.function_note: Sugar plus reduction is literally the same product.

entries.name: White wine (cooking)
entries.role_in_recipes: Acid + depth for deglazing, sauces, risotto, mussels.

subs.name: Broth + white wine vinegar or lemon
subs.use: 1 cup chicken or veg broth + 1/2 Tbsp white wine vinegar or lemon juice
subs.function_note: Broth gives body; vinegar gives the acid.

subs.name: White grape juice + vinegar
subs.use: 1/2 cup white grape juice + 1 Tbsp vinegar + 1/2 cup water
subs.function_note: Grape juice restores the fruit character.

entries.name: Red wine (cooking)
entries.role_in_recipes: Body and depth for braises, bolognese, and pan sauces.

subs.name: Beef broth + red wine vinegar
subs.use: 1 cup beef broth + 1 Tbsp red wine vinegar
subs.function_note: Broth gives body; vinegar gives the acidity.

subs.name: Pomegranate or cranberry juice + vinegar
subs.use: 3/4 cup juice + 1/4 cup water + 1 tsp vinegar
subs.function_note: Tannins and color are close to red wine.

entries.name: Soy sauce
entries.role_in_recipes: Umami and salt in nearly everything savory.

subs.name: Tamari
subs.function_note: Tamari is soy sauce brewed with little or no wheat.

subs.name: Coconut aminos
subs.use: Coconut aminos, 1:1; reduce other sweeteners slightly (it is sweeter)
subs.function_note: Coconut sap carries similar umami.

subs.name: Bragg liquid aminos
subs.function_note: Hydrolyzed soy delivers the same umami compounds.

entries.name: Fish sauce
entries.role_in_recipes: Intense umami-salt backbone for Southeast Asian cooking.

subs.name: Soy sauce + lime juice
subs.use: 1 Tbsp soy sauce + 1 tsp lime juice
subs.function_note: Soy supplies the umami; lime the sharpness.

subs.name: Worcestershire sauce
subs.function_note: Anchovies provide the same fermented-fish umami.

entries.name: Tomato paste
entries.role_in_recipes: Concentrated umami-thickener; brown it in oil for depth.

subs.name: Tomato sauce, simmered down
subs.use: Simmer 1/3 cup tomato sauce until reduced to 1 Tbsp of paste
subs.function_note: Reducing drives off water, concentrating the solids.

subs.name: Ketchup
subs.use: 2 Tbsp ketchup (it is sweeter; skip or halve recipe sugar)
subs.function_note: Ketchup is seasoned tomato concentrate.

entries.name: Chicken broth
entries.role_in_recipes: Savory cooking liquid base for soups, rice, pan sauces.

subs.name: Bouillon cube or granules
subs.use: 1 cube (or 1 tsp granules) dissolved in 1 cup hot water
subs.function_note: The same stock, dehydrated.

subs.name: Vegetable broth
subs.function_note: Different base, same job.

entries.name: Beef broth
entries.role_in_recipes: Deep savory base for braises, gravies, French onion soup.

subs.name: Beef bouillon + water
subs.use: 1 cube (or 1 tsp granules) in 1 cup hot water
subs.function_note: The same stock, dehydrated.

subs.name: Chicken broth + Worcestershire
subs.use: 1 cup chicken broth + 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
subs.function_note: Worcestershire borrows beefy umami.

entries.name: Mayonnaise
entries.role_in_recipes: Emulsified fat: creamy binder for dressings, sandwiches, moist cakes.

subs.name: Greek yogurt
subs.use: 1 cup Greek yogurt (tangier; add 1/2 tsp mustard + a pinch of salt)
subs.function_note: Same creamy role, cultured base.

subs.name: Vegan mayonnaise
subs.function_note: Plant oil and protein make the same emulsion.

subs.name: Mashed avocado
subs.use: 1 cup, with 1 tsp lemon juice to slow browning
subs.function_note: The fat carries the creaminess.

entries.name: Dijon mustard
entries.role_in_recipes: Sharp emulsifier and tang for dressings, marinades, pan sauces.

subs.name: Yellow mustard
subs.use: Yellow mustard, 1:1 + pinch of cayenne to sharpen
subs.function_note: Cayenne restores the bite.

subs.name: Dry mustard powder
subs.use: 1 tsp mustard powder + 2 tsp water + 1 tsp vinegar, rested 10 min
subs.function_note: Powder plus liquid plus acid rebuilds Dijon.

entries.name: Lemon juice
entries.role_in_recipes: Acid: brightens flavor, balances sweetness, sets some desserts.

subs.name: Lime juice
subs.use: 1:1 — the same amount of lime juice
subs.function_note: Same citric acid, different aromatic oils.

subs.name: White vinegar
subs.use: White vinegar, 1:1 in cooking; use 3/4 the amount in dressings
subs.function_note: Acetic acid stands in for citric acid.

subs.name: Citric acid
subs.use: 1/4 tsp citric acid dissolved in 1 Tbsp water
subs.function_note: It is the isolated acid from citrus.

entries.name: Fresh garlic
entries.role_in_recipes: Aromatic base; flavor intensity depends on cut and cook time.

subs.name: Garlic powder
subs.function_note: Dried garlic is concentrated flavor.

subs.name: Jarred minced garlic
subs.function_note: Packed in acid; the flavor is milder.

subs.name: Garlic flakes
subs.use: 1/2 tsp garlic flakes (rehydrate in the dish's liquid)
subs.function_note: Dried; needs moisture to soften.

entries.name: Fresh ginger
entries.role_in_recipes: Bright, peppery heat; essential fresh bite in stir-fries and bakes.

subs.name: Ground ginger
subs.use: 1/4 tsp ground ginger (add early, with the fat/aromatics)
subs.function_note: Drying changes the aromatic oils.

subs.name: Jarred grated ginger
subs.function_note: The closest to fresh.

entries.name: Fresh herbs
entries.role_in_recipes: Aromatics and garnish; fresh is bright, dried is concentrated.

subs.name: Dried herbs
subs.use: 1 tsp dried herbs (add early, with the liquids)
subs.function_note: Drying concentrates the oils about 3:1.

subs.name: Frozen herb cubes or paste (e.g. basil paste)

entries.name: Shallots

subs.name: Red onion, mellowed
subs.use: 1/2 small red onion, minced; soak in cold water 10 min + pinch of sugar
subs.function_note: Soaking pulls out the harsh compounds.

subs.name: Scallions (green onions)
subs.function_note: A milder member of the allium family.

entries.name: Onion
entries.role_in_recipes: Foundation aromatic; sweetens as it cooks.

subs.name: Onion powder
subs.use: 1 Tbsp onion powder (bloom it in hot fat)
subs.function_note: Concentrated dried onion.

subs.name: Leeks
subs.use: 1 large leek, white and light-green parts (sweeter, more delicate)
subs.function_note: A gentler allium.

subs.name: Shallots
subs.use: 2-3 shallots (milder and sweeter — a true upgrade, not just a stand-in)
subs.function_note: A refined allium — you won't miss the onion.

entries.name: Ghee

subs.name: DIY clarified butter
subs.use: Melt 1 cup butter gently 15 min; skim foam; pour off the golden liquid, leave milky solids
subs.function_note: You are making ghee: milk solids removed.

subs.name: Neutral oil + optional pinch of salt
subs.function_note: Same smoke point, no dairy notes.

entries.name: Coconut milk

subs.name: Heavy cream + coconut extract

subs.name: Light coconut milk
subs.use: 1 cup light coconut milk + 1 tsp oil if richness matters
subs.function_note: Less fat; add oil for body.

entries.name: Ricotta
entries.role_in_recipes: Light, grainy fresh cheese for lasagna, cannoli, pancakes.

subs.name: Cottage cheese, blended smooth
subs.use: 1 cup small-curd cottage cheese, blended 30 s

subs.name: Mascarpone thinned with milk
subs.function_note: Higher fat, finer texture.

entries.name: Unsweetened chocolate

entries.name: Shortening

subs.name: Coconut oil
subs.function_note: The same solid 100% fat behavior.

entries.name: Applesauce
entries.role_in_recipes: Moisture + mild sweetness; fat and egg replacer in quick bakes.

subs.name: Mashed banana

subs.name: Pumpkin purée
subs.function_note: The same moisture content.

subs.name: Plain yogurt

entries.name: Gelatin

subs.name: Agar-agar powder

entries.name: Hoisin sauce
